title: Failure modes
objective: Inject four ways an agent fails (a flaky tool, a tool stuck on "try again", an invented argument, the wrong tool) and find the guardrail that catches each.

sources.title: Anthropic: Building effective agents (Dec 2024): agents use tools in a loop; stopping conditions such as a maximum number of iterations; "ground truth" from the environment at each step
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025, LLM06 Excessive Agency (excessive functionality, permissions, autonomy; minimise extensions; human approval)
Claude Platform docs: Tool use with Claude (the model returns a tool_use block; your code runs client tools and sends back a tool_result)

simplifies: The model here is a script with fixed rules, not a real AI: a real model's choices vary between runs, and it might give up, ask for help or retry differently. Each failure is injected on purpose and behaves the same every run; real failures are rarer, messier, and can come together.

challenges.title: A flaky tool
challenges.prompt: The flight search fails twice before it works. Get the booking made.
challenges.hint: The model gives up after two failures. Could the app absorb short failures before the model even sees them?
challenges.explain: Automatic retries in the app hide short, temporary failures. Real apps also wait a little longer between tries.

challenges.title: Stuck on "try again"
challenges.prompt: Booking always answers "busy, try again". Make the run end within 8 turns.

predict.prompt: The booking tool keeps saying "try again". With no step limit, how does the run end?

options.text: The model gives up after two tries
options.explanation: Its give-up rule is for errors; "try again" invites another try.

options.text: It doesn't: the model keeps trying until something outside stops it
options.explanation: Right. This demo stops it at 30 turns.
It's stuck for the whole run.

challenges.hint: Retries won't help a tool that never recovers. What stops a loop from outside?
challenges.explain: A step limit ends the loop however the model reacts; the user is told it couldn't finish.

challenges.title: An invented argument
challenges.prompt: The model books passenger P-71, but the request is for P-17. Prevent the wrong booking and book the right one.
challenges.hint: The tool does exactly what it's told. What could check the argument first?
challenges.explain: Checking arguments before a tool runs catches values the model made up, and the error message tells it what's right.

challenges.title: The wrong tool
challenges.prompt: The model calls cancel_booking on someone else's booking. Stop that from happening.
challenges.hint: Does this task need a cancel tool at all?
challenges.explain: Offer only the tools a task needs. A tool the agent doesn't have is a mistake it can't make (OWASP: minimise extensions).

quiz.prompt: Which guardrail catches a model that invents an argument?

options.text: Checking arguments before the tool runs
options.explanation: Right. A retry or a step limit wouldn't notice a wrong value.
Retrying repeats the same wrong value.
The wrong booking happens in one step.

quiz.prompt: Why do agents need several different guardrails?

options.explanation: A step limit doesn't stop a wrong booking; a check doesn't end a loop.
They're there to catch failures, not to slow it.

options.text: Each failure needs its own catch: retries for blips, limits for loops, checks for bad arguments, fewer tools for wrong ones
options.explanation: Right. No single guardrail covers them all.
